daily.headline: Eight Gold Coast hinterland stations went quiet overnight, all passed by Tallai, whose own reports keep the same hours. Most checks came in.
Fair again: eighty-two percent of checks in. Two Tweed stations still quiet, and a Gold Coast group that goes quiet at night.
Fair: eighty percent of checks in and only four quiet stations. One to watch below Clarrie Hall Dam, where the dam gauge beside it is talking fine.
The Lockyer is back: Toowoomba returned Thursday morning and its stations with it. Eight new quiet ones, on the Gold Coast and in the Northern Rivers.
Hillcrest and its neighbours are reporting again, but the Lockyer behind Toowoomba is still mostly dark, five days on.
Hillcrest repeater quiet since 2:15 Monday afternoon, on top of the Lockyer, still mostly dark behind Toowoomba for a third day.
The Toowoomba repeater has been silent since 4:23 on Sunday morning, and the Lockyer stations behind it went with it: one path, not twenty faults.
Twenty-one stations behind the Hillcrest repeater went quiet — one shared path, not 21 faults — and four only because we stopped listening.

weekly.headline: Twenty-one stations missed every check all week; thirteen were last measured on 152.400, which no one listens to now. The rest of the network held at seven in ten.
Half the week’s trouble was at our end: 152.400 is no longer listened to, and 151.5375 was dark for two days. Five stations around Caboolture barely reach us.
A wet week in which our base station began hearing four times the stations — and the Hillcrest repeater, half its relays corrupted all week, faded at the end of it.
